title: Gesture to unlock the screen
line: The lock screen can now be unlocked by drawing a pattern through a 3×3 grid of dots, like on a phone.
explanation: The lock screen could only be unlocked with the password (or fingerprint, smartcard and similar devices); there was no way to draw a pattern as on phones. kscreenlocker now has a Pattern unlock method next to Smartcard, Face and U2F, using a new kde-pattern PAM service, and the lock screen shows a 3×3 grid of dots when it is selected. Drawing through the dots (or typing their numbers and pressing Enter) sends their digits, 1 to 9 row by row, to that PAM service, and the Password method stays available as before.

commits.message:
greeter: add a Pattern authenticator

There was no way to unlock by drawing a pattern, as on phones. Add a
Pattern method next to Smartcard and Face, which answers the new
kde-pattern PAM service with the digits of the dots that were drawn.

BUG: 455672

lockscreen: add a pattern pad for the Pattern authenticator

Choosing the new Pattern unlock method left only an empty space, as the
lock screen has just a password field. Show a 3×3 grid of dots for it:
drawing through them, or typing their numbers, unlocks the screen.

BUG: 455672

patches.diff:
From 9747e5c75e34449e3d3b10416d2b7a21e51bed1a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 23:46:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] greeter: add a Pattern authenticator

There was no way to unlock by drawing a pattern, as on phones. Add a
Pattern method next to Smartcard and Face, which answers the new
kde-pattern PAM service with the digits of the dots that were drawn.

BUG: 455672
---
 README.pam                        | 7 +++++++
 greeter/pamauthenticatormodel.cpp | 8 ++++++++
 greeter/pamauthenticators.cpp     | 2 ++
 greeter/pamauthenticators.h       | 1 +
 greeter/worker/CMakeLists.txt     | 5 +++++
 greeter/worker/config-worker.h.in | 3 +++
 6 files changed, 26 insertions(+)

diff --git a/README.pam b/README.pam
index 9c11a7ae..db5ffded 100644
--- a/README.pam
+++ b/README.pam
@@ -48,6 +48,13 @@ configuration files and PAM documentation on your system for guidance as
 to what entries to make.  If you call a PAM service that is not
 configured, the default action of PAM is likely to be denial of service.
 
+Unlocking by drawing a pattern uses the PAM service "kde-pattern"
+(-DKSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE=<service>, "disabled" to turn it off).
+Users enable it with Pattern=true in the [Authenticators] group of
+kscreenlockerrc. The drawn pattern is answered to the service's prompt as
+the digits of the dots it passes through, numbered 1 to 9 row by row from
+the top left, so any module that checks a per-user PIN can verify it.
+
 Note: Screen lockers typically only authenticate a user to allow her to
 continue working. They may also renew tokens etc., where supported.
 See the Linux PAM Administrators guide, which is part of the PAM
diff --git a/greeter/pamauthenticatormodel.cpp b/greeter/pamauthenticatormodel.cpp
index 011a8e68..bb5eeaa4 100644
--- a/greeter/pamauthenticatormodel.cpp
+++ b/greeter/pamauthenticatormodel.cpp
@@ -37,6 +37,7 @@ namespace
     constexpr auto faceEnabled = isStaticallyEnabled(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_FACE_SERVICE);
     constexpr auto universal2factorEnabled = isStaticallyEnabled(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE);
     constexpr auto smartcardEnabled = isStaticallyEnabled(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_SMARTCARD_SERVICE);
+    constexpr auto patternEnabled = isStaticallyEnabled(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE);
 
     KConfig config(u"kscreenlockerrc"_s);
     const auto authenticators = config.group(u"Authenticators"_s);
@@ -81,6 +82,13 @@ namespace
             false,
             i18nc("authentication type in unlock dialogs - universal 2 factor authentication (yubikey etc)", "Universal 2 Factor"),
             true),
+        std::make_shared<PAMAuthenticatorDescriptor>(patternEnabled && authenticators.readEntry("Pattern", false),
+                                                     PamAuthenticators::Authenticator::Pattern,
+                                                     u"view-app-grid-symbolic"_s,
+                                                     false,
+                                                     true,
+                                                     i18nc("authentication type in unlock dialogs - drawing a pattern through a grid of dots", "Pattern"),
+                                                     false),
     };
 
     auto view = all | std::views::filter([](const auto &d) {
diff --git a/greeter/pamauthenticators.cpp b/greeter/pamauthenticators.cpp
index e46392c1..eab8fb74 100644
--- a/greeter/pamauthenticators.cpp
+++ b/greeter/pamauthenticators.cpp
@@ -189,6 +189,8 @@ void PamAuthenticators::onAuthenticatorChanged()
             return make_unique(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_FACE_SERVICE, PamAuthenticator::Face);
         case Authenticator::Universal2Factor:
             return make_unique(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE, PamAuthenticator::Universal2Factor);
+        case Authenticator::Pattern:
+            return make_unique(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE, PamAuthenticator::None);
         }
         Q_ASSERT_X(false, Q_FUNC_INFO, "unhandled authenticator type");
         return std::unique_ptr<PamAuthenticator>{};
diff --git a/greeter/pamauthenticators.h b/greeter/pamauthenticators.h
index a12105d5..57ad1dd5 100644
--- a/greeter/pamauthenticators.h
+++ b/greeter/pamauthenticators.h
@@ -53,6 +53,7 @@ public:
         Smartcard,
         Face,
         Universal2Factor,
+        Pattern,
     };
     Q_ENUM(Authenticator)
 
diff --git a/greeter/worker/CMakeLists.txt b/greeter/worker/CMakeLists.txt
index 5d65e80e..fd738052 100644
--- a/greeter/worker/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/greeter/worker/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -23,6 +23,10 @@ if(CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 4.2)
         TYPE STRING
         HELP "The PAM service to use for universal 2-factor authentication. 'disabled' to disable"
         VALUE "kde-u2f")
+    set(CACHE{KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE}
+        TYPE STRING
+        HELP "The PAM service to use for pattern authentication. 'disabled' to disable"
+        VALUE "kde-pattern")
 else()
     # This can be dropped once our FreeBSD CI has 4.2+ (which should be around Plasma 6.9)
     set(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PASSWORD_SERVICE "kde" CACHE STRING "The PAM service to use for password authentication. CANNOT be disabled!")
@@ -30,6 +34,7 @@ else()
     set(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_SMARTCARD_SERVICE "kde-smartcard" CACHE STRING "The PAM service to use for smartcard authentication. 'disabled' to disable")
     set(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_FACE_SERVICE "kde-face" CACHE STRING "The PAM service to use for face authentication. 'disabled' to disable")
     set(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE "kde-u2f" CACHE STRING "The PAM service to use for universal 2-factor authentication. 'disabled' to disable")
+    set(KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE "kde-pattern" CACHE STRING "The PAM service to use for pattern authentication. 'disabled' to disable")
 endif()
 
 configure_file(config-worker.h.in ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/config-worker.h)
diff --git a/greeter/worker/config-worker.h.in b/greeter/worker/config-worker.h.in
index df26e934..dcb337f7 100644
--- a/greeter/worker/config-worker.h.in
+++ b/greeter/worker/config-worker.h.in
@@ -19,3 +19,6 @@ static_assert(!KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_FACE_SERVICE.isEmpty(), "KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_FACE
 
 constexpr auto KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE = QLatin1String("@KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE@");
 static_assert(!KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE.isEmpty(), "KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_UNIVERSAL2FACTOR_SERVICE must be defined");
+
+constexpr auto KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE = QLatin1String("@KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE@");
+static_assert(!KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE.isEmpty(), "KSCREENLOCKER_PAM_PATTERN_SERVICE must be defined");
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Before: even with Pattern=true in kscreenlockerrc, the lock screen only offers the password field.
After: a Pattern button appears next to Password and shows a 3×3 grid of dots.
After: a wrong pattern shows "Unlocking failed" and clears the grid; drawing the right one unlocks.
